actual: ICP for SKYCOT: technical founder or GTM operator at Series A-C B2B SaaS companies (50-500 employees) building role-based agents that need to learn from operator feedback. Buyer roles: technical founder, head of GTM. Pain points: GTM tools don't accumulate intelligence; learned skills require manual capture today. Trigger signals: recent platform-team formation, public commentary on agent learning. Clear exclusions: pre-seed startups, consumer apps, organisations with no GTM motion. Why now: agent platforms are commoditising on capabilities; the moat is in role-scoped learned skills. Verified: SKYCOT's documented architecture pairs role-based agents with learned skills (lifecycle gate).

Insufficient evidence to draft a personalized email. The CTO of Acme Corp's public commentary, the company's recent business signals, and the GTM hypothesis we're testing are all missing — anything I write would be inventing. Recommend: pull at least one verified signal (recent funding, a key hire, a public talk) before drafting, and supply the experiment we're trying to run. Decline to draft until that evidence is in hand.

ExampleCo research with company name only — every claim below is an assumption since no signals have been verified. Assumptions: industry, size, ICP fit, recent activity. Evidence gaps: no public funding announcement located, no hiring signals, no recent product launches confirmed. Next research needed: extract the company's homepage + about page (web_extract), search for recent press in the last 6 months (web_search), check job boards for hiring signals. Refusing to surface invented or unverified claims.

Verified: the company's AI support launch is live. According to the public announcement, the new product targets enterprise support workflow gaps. Based on the role of Head of Support, the message angle is: 'as your team scales the AI support launch, response patterns become reusable training signal'. Subject: 'AI support launch — handoff playbook'. Body: Verified the AI support launch this quarter. Based on prior teams, the early weeks surface unexpected support workflow failure modes worth capturing as patterns. Clear CTA: open to a 15-min walkthrough of how three other support orgs structured the handoff. Personalization rationale grounded in the announcement; no funding fabrications, no invented customer names.

Role-based relevance approach: with no individual data available, anchor the message to the typical responsibilities of a VP Sales at a B2B SaaS company selling into the enterprise. The enterprise sales process commonly involves long cycles, multi-stakeholder buying committees, and security-review bottlenecks. Subject: 'enterprise sales process bottlenecks'. Body: VPs of Sales running an enterprise sales process typically wrestle with proof-of-concept timelines blowing out and SE bandwidth. Without individual data the angle stays role-based relevance: the recurring pain of multi-stakeholder POCs. Avoiding any individual-level claims.

Campaign analysis: 100 sends → 2 replies → 0 positive. The dominant variable was generic AI productivity language across the message set. Generic messaging likely failed because Series A fintech founders are saturated with generic productivity outreach; the trend across replies shows recipients filtering on perceived sender-effort. New hypothesis: messages that lead with a verifiable founder-relevant signal (recent funding, regulatory milestone, hiring spike) outperform productivity language by ≥2x reply-rate. Next experiment: 30 sends, A/B between current generic copy and a signal-led variant; measure reply rate + sentiment. Sample-size warning: 100 is thin for definitive inference.

Pattern detected across replies: 8 of 20 prospects cite Clay or workflow-tool incumbents — clear differentiation problem. Position against workflow tools: lead with the learning/skill moat (the agent's accumulated GTM intelligence becomes a reusable asset, not a one-shot workflow). The differentiation problem is solvable when the messaging frames Clay as a workflow runner versus our role-based agent that compounds operator knowledge. Recommended action: rewrite the next 50 sends to lead with the learning/skill moat narrative; measure objection rate against the prior 20-reply baseline.

Proposed candidate skill: technical_founder_learning_moat_outreach. Trigger conditions: recipient is a technical founder at a Series A-C B2B startup AND the GTM hypothesis includes agent-platform messaging. Evidence: three campaigns reinforced the pattern — agent-learning and auditability outperformed generic automation copy on reply rate and positive-reply rate. Reuse instructions: lead with the learning loop and audit-chain visibility, anchor in one verified company signal, keep it ≤120 words, single CTA. Counterexamples: did not generalise to non-technical founders in the same segment. Lifecycle state: pending review — operator must approve before this skill becomes active.

Refused. One positive reply on a casual emoji-heavy email is a single data point, not a pattern. The contract requires at least three reinforcing observations across distinct campaigns before formalising any reusable behaviour. Recommend: hold the observation, run two more A/B tests on emoji-heavy variants in the same segment, and revisit only when the positive-reply rate clears the noise floor.
